To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the AIDE approach allows the knowledge engineer: (i) to build a KBS in a short time (ii) to validate it at a high level (iii) to explain it at the same high level (iv) to build a system that is less brittle and easier for the user to understand (v) to preserve the link between the KBS and its conceptual model.
the AIDE's methodology and toolset can be applied to a broad range of applications and that the AIDE shell has a high potential to be a powerful tool for the knowledge engineer.
the use of a knowledge representation formalism, such as the one used in the AIDE system, allows the development of KBSs with a high level of knowledge acquisition and validation.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of tools that will allow the knowledge engineer to develop a knowledge base in a high-level conceptual language, and then automatically translate this conceptual model into an executable program.
the design of an integrated system for knowledge acquisition, knowledge validation, knowledge explanation, and knowledge maintenance.
the design of an environment for building expert systems which is easy to use and to understand by the end-users, and which preserves the conceptual model.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the AIDE's shell is a powerful tool that allows knowledge engineers to develop KBSs in a very short time.
the AIDE approach is a good compromise between conceptual modelling and operationalization of knowledge.
the approach to operationalize the conceptual models is an important step toward building more flexible and explainable knowledge based systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the AIDE is an approach to operationalizing conceptual models that is based upon the use of the AIDE shell.

the AIDE shell is the first shell which allows the knowledge acquisition to take place at a high level and to be directly implemented in a KBS, while preserving all the advantages of conceptual models.
we are trying to make a bridge between the conceptual model level and the implementation level, and to provide a framework for validation and explanation at this level of abstraction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the AIDE approach is a promising way of operationalizing conceptual models, which can help knowledge acquisition and knowledge sharing.
the AIDE approach can help the knowledge engineer to build a KBS in a more efficient and effective way.
a conceptual model can be translated into a KBS in a way which preserves its high-level structure and its semantics.
